prompt.context_jp: その窓口の一つに、若い行員の花咲舞___座っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: その窓口の一つに、若い行員の花咲舞___座っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces Mai as new information in the scene.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is introducing Hanasaki Mai for the first time — a classic new-information setup, so が marks her as the newly presented subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat Mai as an already-known topic, which doesn't fit her first appearance. を doesn't fit an intransitive verb like 座る.

contrast_examples.jp: 窓口に若い行員が座っていた。
contrast_examples.en: A young clerk was sitting at the counter. (new info)
That clerk is Hanasaki Mai. (already known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 舞___背筋を伸ばし、次の客を迎える準備を整えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞___背筋を伸ばし、次の客を迎える準備を整えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: Mai has just been introduced; now she is the ongoing topic.

feedback.correct_en: Mai was just introduced in the previous sentence; she is now the established topic. は carries the narrative along with her as the theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would re-introduce her as new, which is unnecessary. に doesn't fit as a subject marker.

prompt.context_jp: そこで待っていたのは、この支店で長く働く先輩の根津___。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこで待っていた___、この支店で長く働く先輩の根津だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the cleft-like 'the one who was waiting was Nezu' structure.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence frames 'the one waiting there' as the known topic and reveals Nezu as new. のは…だった is the standard cleft pattern here.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would shift emphasis to selecting the subject exhaustively, which doesn't match the narrative revelation.

contrast_examples.jp: 待っていたのは根津だった。

prompt.context_jp: 根津___規則や手順に誰よりも厳しく、どんな小さなことも見逃さない人として知られている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 根津___規則や手順に誰よりも厳しく、見逃さない人として知られている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing a general description of Nezu.

feedback.correct_en: This sentence describes Nezu's general character — a classic topic-comment with は. The sentence tells us 'as for Nezu, she is known for…'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark her as new or exhaustively identified, which clashes with the generic description that follows.

contrast_examples.en: Nezu is the one in charge. (exhaustive identification)

prompt.context_jp: 「今朝の支店長室の清掃 花咲さん___担当ですよね？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「今朝の支店長室の清掃 花咲さん___担当ですよね？」
prompt.prompt_en: Nezu is confirming WHO specifically is in charge. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Nezu is pinpointing Mai specifically as the one in charge — an exhaustive-listing/identification use of が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a general statement about Mai, not an identification of the responsible person.

contrast_examples.en: Hanasaki is the one in charge. (identifying)
As for Hanasaki, she's in charge. (describing)

prompt.context_jp: 「この花___支店長室には飾れません｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「この花___支店長室には飾れません｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Nezu rejects specifically THIS flower (implying others might be OK). Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は carries a contrastive nuance here: 'THIS flower (as opposed to acceptable ones) can't be displayed.' It picks out the flower as the topic being rejected.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the flower as new info, missing the contrast with implicitly acceptable flowers.

contrast_examples.en: This flower can't be displayed (others might be OK).

prompt.context_jp: 「決まりというのは 守り続けること___意味があるんです｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「守り続けること___意味があるんです｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'there is meaning IN continuing to uphold'.

feedback.correct_en: 〜に意味がある ('there is meaning in ~') uses に to mark the locus where the meaning resides.
feedback.incorrect_en: を doesn't work with ある. で would mark means/location of an action, not where meaning inheres.

contrast_examples.en: Study at school. (で = location of action)

prompt.context_jp: 「簡単じゃなくても 誰か___声を上げなければ 何も変わらないんじゃ ないでしょうか｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「誰か___声を上げなければ 何も変わらない｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'if SOMEONE doesn't speak up, nothing will change.'

feedback.correct_en: 誰か (indefinite 'someone') is new, unspecified information, so it takes が. Indefinite pronouns like 誰か almost always take が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰かは is ungrammatical here because 誰か is not a known topic — it refers to any unspecified person.

prompt.context_jp: 「舞___うちの支店のエースだよ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「舞___うちの支店のエースだよ｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: Miyu is characterizing Mai with a predicate noun.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for Mai, she's our branch's ace' — a characterizing statement about a known person uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'who is the ace?' (exhaustive). Here Miyu is describing Mai, not picking her out from alternatives.

prompt.context_jp: 誰かと組んで動くより、一人で気楽に過ごすほう___性に合っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一人で気楽に過ごすほう___性に合っている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'the option of spending time alone is what suits me.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜ほうが性に合っている is a fixed comparative pattern — が marks the preferred/selected option exhaustively.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken the comparison. With 〜より…ほう, が is the natural partner.

contrast_examples.jp: こっちのほうが好きだ。

prompt.context_jp: どんな人___待っているのか、舞は何も聞かされていなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: どんな人___待っているのか、舞は何も聞かされていなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the embedded question 'what kind of person was waiting'.

feedback.correct_en: In WH-questions (どんな人, 誰, 何), the unknown subject takes が because it's unidentified new information.
feedback.incorrect_en: どんな人は is ungrammatical — question-word subjects can't be topics with は.

prompt.context_jp:
「彼女は異例だよ｡ あの紀本部長の懐刀だから｡」
「未来の頭取候補の1人だよ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「彼女___異例だよ｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: Souma is characterizing Reiko ('as for her, she's exceptional').

feedback.correct_en: Souma is making a general comment ABOUT Reiko who was just mentioned — は picks her up as the topic for description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'who is exceptional?' which isn't the point here.

prompt.context_jp: 「ごめん 課長___臨店の人と余計なことは話すな って言われてるから｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「課長___臨店の人と余計なことは話すな って言われてるから｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'I was told by the manager not to…'

feedback.correct_en: から marks the source of the instruction in passive 'be told' constructions. 課長から言われる = 'told by the manager'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the manager as subject of 言う (active), but the sentence is 言われている (passive)—we need the source marker.

contrast_examples.en: I was warned by the manager.

prompt.context_jp: 「だから 嫌われる｡ つまり 誰___やりたがらない みんなが嫌がる仕事ってことだ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「誰___やりたがらない｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'NO ONE wants to do it.'

feedback.correct_en: 誰も + negative = 'no one'. This is the fixed quantifier pattern for universal negation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰は is ungrammatical. 誰が with a negative would ask a rhetorical question, not state 'no one'.

prompt.context_jp: 「これって内部告発ですよね？ いや～ いたずらだろ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「これ___内部告発ですよね？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: Mai is identifying the paper AS a whistleblower letter.

feedback.correct_en: これって is colloquial for これは — Mai is making 'this (paper)' the topic and asking what it is. Natural spoken Japanese.
feedback.incorrect_en: これが would awkwardly identify 'this' as answering 'which is the leak?' which doesn't match the context.

prompt.context_jp: 「藤枝支店長の個人口座 特に怪しい金の動き___ないそうだ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「特に怪しい金の動き___ないそうだ｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'no suspicious money movements, in particular.'

feedback.correct_en: With negation ('ない'), the subject often takes は to signal contrast: suspicious movements specifically are absent (other movements may exist).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be a flat statement; は with a negative is the natural way to say 'not this particular thing'.

contrast_examples.en: I don't have money. (contrast: other things exist)

prompt.context_jp: 「赴任して間もなく 2億の長期運転資金の融資___実行されてるんだな｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「2億の長期運転資金の融資___実行されてるんだな｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: Souma just discovered this fact in the records.

feedback.correct_en: Souma is noting a newly discovered fact from the documents — the loan is new information surfacing as he reads. が marks the newly observed event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the loan as already-known topic, but Souma is just discovering it.

contrast_examples.jp: 融資が実行されている。
その融資は実行済みだ。
contrast_examples.en: That loan has been executed. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 根津に反論する直前の場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あの…｡ ___ようですが 昔からの決まりを そのまま守り続けることが 必ずしも正しいとは 思えないんですが｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Mai's signature line before contradicting a superior politely.

feedback.correct_en: お言葉を返すようですが is a formal set phrase meaning 'I hate to contradict you, but…' — Mai's trademark line in the series.
feedback.incorrect_en: 口を挟む means 'to butt in' and 話を切る isn't a standard polite preface for disagreement.

contrast_examples.jp: お言葉を返すようですが、違います。
contrast_examples.en: I hate to contradict you, but it's different.
I don't want to butt in, but… (different nuance)

prompt.context_jp: 根津がマイに警告する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「若いからといって 調子に乗ってると いつか___に遭いますよ｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom: 'you'll regret it / learn a painful lesson.'

feedback.correct_en: 痛い目に遭う is the fixed idiom meaning 'to have a bitter/painful experience.' Nezu is warning Mai she'll suffer for her boldness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 痛い顔 and 痛い手 are not idioms. Only 目 is used in this expression.

prompt.context_jp: 玲子についての説明。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「彼女は異例だよ｡ あの紀本部長の___だから｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word: 'she's the department head's right-hand person'.

feedback.correct_en: 懐刀 (ふところがたな) literally 'dagger in the breast' = a trusted right-hand person/confidant. It's the standard idiom in corporate contexts.
feedback.incorrect_en: 右手 is literally 'right hand' but isn't used idiomatically this way in Japanese. 腹心友 isn't a word.

prompt.context_jp: 相馬が臨店の仕事を説明する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「本部の人間が ノコノコやって来て ___の隅 チクチク つつき回すようなまねされて 面白いわけないだろ｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word to complete this idiom about nitpicking.

feedback.correct_en: 重箱の隅をつつく (literally 'poke the corners of a lacquer box') is the fixed idiom for nitpicking at trivial details.
feedback.incorrect_en: 弁当 and 茶碗 aren't used in this idiom. Only 重箱 appears here.

prompt.context_jp: 相馬が臨店の心得を説明する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「余計なことは 見ざる 言わざる ___｡ それが臨店の極意だ｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the 'three monkeys' set phrase.

feedback.correct_en: 見ざる・言わざる・聞かざる are the proverbial Three Wise Monkeys: 'see no, speak no, hear no' (evil). Souma is quoting this fixed trio.
feedback.incorrect_en: 知らざる and 見せざる don't belong to this well-known idiomatic set.

contrast_examples.jp: 見ざる言わざる聞かざる
contrast_examples.en: see no evil, speak no evil, hear no evil

prompt.context_jp: 舞が健に新しい仕事を愚痴る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「支店の人たちから ___仕事でさぁ｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word: 'a job that the branch people find annoying/unwelcome.'

feedback.correct_en: 煙たがる means to find someone unpleasant/to be avoided (like smoke); 煙たがられる is the passive 'to be treated as unwelcome'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 重たがられる and 苦しがられる aren't standard; 煙たい is the fixed metaphor for unwelcome presence.

contrast_examples.en: to be treated as unwelcome by the boss

prompt.context_jp: 健が舞に言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あのなぁ ___言ってると 追い出すぞ｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom meaning 'if you keep complaining about this and that…'

feedback.correct_en: 四の五の言う is the fixed idiom meaning 'to complain / grumble about this and that.' The numbers 4-5 are fixed.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一の二の and 六の七の are not idioms; only 四の五の is used.

prompt.context_jp: 相馬が怪しい支払いについてコメントする場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「こういう ___数字ってのはな 通常の取引では あまり出てこない｡」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase meaning 'a round number'.

feedback.correct_en: 切りがいい/切りのいい means 'a nice round number' or 'a convenient stopping point.' It's the idiomatic phrase for suspiciously clean figures.
feedback.incorrect_en: 丸いまま and 端のない aren't standard expressions for round numbers in Japanese.

prompt.context_jp: Mai has just been introduced in the previous sentence.
prompt.prompt_en: Which continuation sounds most natural as narrative flow after introducing Mai?

choices.text: 舞は背筋を伸ばし、次の客を迎える準備を整えた。
舞が背筋を伸ばし、次の客を迎える準備を整えた。
舞も背筋を伸ばし、次の客を迎える準備を整えた。

feedback.correct_en: Since Mai was just introduced, she is now the discourse topic. は carries the narrative smoothly forward.
feedback.incorrect_en: が re-introduces her as new (odd right after her introduction). も implies 'Mai too' which has no antecedent here.

prompt.context_jp: The 臨店 team asking a busy branch manager for cooperation.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural when asking a superior for cooperation?

choices.text: お忙しいところ恐縮ですが、ご協力お願いいたします。
忙しそうですけど、協力してください。
忙しくても、協力しなさい。

feedback.correct_en: お忙しいところ恐縮ですが is the standard business-polite preface, pairing naturally with お願いいたします for a respectful request.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too casual for addressing a branch manager. C uses a command form (〜しなさい) which is disrespectful upward.

contrast_examples.jp: 恐れ入りますが、ご確認ください。

prompt.context_jp: Mai ordering at her uncle's casual izakaya after the shopkeeper teased her about her first phrasing.
prompt.prompt_en: Which order sounds most natural in a casual izakaya?

choices.text: おいしいビールと今日のオススメ下さい。
おいしきビールと今日のオススメを頂戴いたしたく。
ビールのおいしいのと今日オススメが下さいませ。

feedback.correct_en: A is the natural, casual order register that fits a bar/izakaya. The word order and politeness level match the setting.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses overly stiff written-formal grammar. C has awkward word order and mismatched politeness.

contrast_examples.jp: ビールを頂戴できますでしょうか。
contrast_examples.en: May I have a beer? (overly formal)

prompt.context_jp: Mai pushes back against Nezu's rigid defense of old rules.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for 'if no one speaks up, nothing will change'?

choices.text: 誰かが声を上げなければ、何も変わらない。
誰かは声を上げなければ、何も変わらない。
誰かも声を上げなければ、何も変わらない。

feedback.correct_en: Indefinite 誰か pairs with が, not は. 'If someone (unspecified) doesn't speak up' sounds natural only with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰かは is ungrammatical because indefinites can't serve as topic. 誰かも doesn't convey the intended meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: あの人は助けてくれる。

prompt.context_jp: Mai argues that the whistleblower must not be abandoned.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'the person who spoke up will be left suffering'?

choices.text: 声を上げてくれた人が苦しんだままになっちゃう。
声を出してくれた人が苦しんだままになっちゃう。
声を言ってくれた人が苦しんだままになっちゃう。

feedback.correct_en: 声を上げる is the standard collocation for 'to speak up / raise one's voice (in protest).' It fits the whistleblower context perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 声を出す is literal 'make a sound' and lacks the protest nuance. 声を言う isn't a natural collocation.
